Customer to share 2GB representative dataset and success criteria doc by 2025-12-08
Schedule follow-up meeting to review benchmark results week of 2025-12-15

summary: POC scoping focused on selecting an open-model shortlist for a multilingual genomics annotation assistant. Discussed success metrics (exact match / macro-F1 / latency), workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline for 3-week pilot, and security questions around data residency and KMS.
transcript:
Meeting Header: 2025-12-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Park (Orchid), Akash Patel (Orchid CTO), Ruth Gomez (Orchid PM)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. we're here to scope the POC — model shortlist, benchmarks, and timeline. quick roll call?
[00:07] Dr. Lena Park: lena here.
[00:09] Akash Patel: akash, hi.
[00:10] Ruth Gomez: ruth, thanks.
[00:15] Carlos Rivera: carlos from redwood, i'll be running the bench.
[00:20] Maya Chen: cool. quick context from orchid? ruth or lena do you want to set the scene for what success looks like?
[00:27] Ruth Gomez: sure. our goal is an assistant to annotate genomic variants and surface likely impacts, basically reduce manual triage. success metric for us is accuracy on a 200-item labeled set, target macro-F1 > 0.78 and median latency under 600ms at 8 concurrent users. cost is also a constraint — we want sub-$0.015 per request average if possible.
[00:46] Dr. Lena Park: also need good support for Spanish and Korean — clinicians in Spain and Korea will use it. domain: clinical genomics, lots of abbreviations and structured outputs.
[00:58] Maya Chen: great, that helps. on Redwood side, we usually test 3 model flavors for open POCs: a smaller fast quantized model, a middle ground fp16 model, and a larger instruction-tuned model. examples we suggested in the prep note were: LlamaX-7b-quant, Mistral-11B-fp16, and OpenGG-13B-instruct. any red flags with those?
[01:20] Akash Patel: quick question — licensing for open models is fine, but we need to confirm export controls, nothing sensitive leaves our EU VPC. can you do VPC-only runs?
[01:29] Carlos Rivera: yes, for the dedicated/private POC we can run in your VPC or our private connector. for the hosted bench we can run sanitized samples. we'll put data residency constraints in the bench plan.
[01:38] Ruth Gomez: on model choices — we worry about hallucination on clinical inference. bigger models might be better for reasoning but cost and latency go up.
[01:47] Maya Chen: totally, that's the tradeoff we'll measure. for hallucination we typically use a combination of deterministic scoring against your labeled set and a reranker step; we can include a rerank model in the pipeline for improved precision.
[01:59] [01:59] -- TIMESTAMP --
[02:00] Carlos Rivera: i want to confirm workload sizing. ruth, you mentioned 8 concurrent users. what's your p95 token length? do we have typical prompts?
[02:08] Ruth Gomez: median prompt is 120 tokens, full context with patient history can go up to 900 tokens, though that's less common. output is usually 60–120 tokens structured JSON.
[02:20] Carlos Rivera: got it. for benching i'll simulate 8 conc with the token distribution: 60% short (<=150), 30% medium (150-400), 10% long (>400). that will affect batching and KV cache behaviour.
[02:33] Dr. Lena Park: one more — we need deterministic structured fields: severity: {low, moderate, high}, recommended action, evidence citations. is Redwood's structured output support good?
[02:43] Maya Chen: yes we have function-calling style outputs and schema enforcement. Carlos can set up eval metrics to check schema compliance and validate citations against provided reference docs.
[02:52] Akash Patel: about benchmarks — can you show latency, cost per 1k tokens, and quality metrics in the same report? we need to justify choice to compliance team.
[03:01] Carlos Rivera: yes we'll produce a benchmark matrix: latency p50/p90, cost per 1k tokens, exact match/macro-F1 on labeled set, and hallucination rate (false statements per 100 responses). we'll run each model with quant and fp16 when available.
[03:15] Ruth Gomez: do you support mixed-precision / quantization profiles? in earlier conversations i saw options like int8 and q4_0.
[03:22] Carlos Rivera: we support q4_0, q4_1, int8 on supported models and we document quality deltas. we'll include quantized runs for the smaller model and fp16 for midsize.
[03:32] [03:32] -- 15-MINUTE MARK --
[03:33] Maya Chen: timeline proposal: data and success criteria by next monday (2025-12-08), Redwood runs bench 3–4 days (ends by 2025-12-12), review meeting week of 2025-12-15, then decision on pilot. does that align?
[03:45] Akash Patel: timeline works. legal will want SOC2 and data processing addendum before any private runs.
[03:53] Maya Chen: we've got SOC 2 Type II and we can share the DPA template. we'll flag that as part of pre-pilot checklist.
[04:01] Dr. Lena Park: sensitive items — we'll sanitize direct patient identifiers but still consider the dataset PHI-ish. KMS integration is required for any private deployment.
[04:10] Carlos Rivera: ok we'll include KMS/HSM options in the notes and outline flow for ephemeral credentials.
[04:16] Ruth Gomez: on evaluation metrics — macro-F1 target 0.78, but we also want human-in-the-loop fallback for edge cases. can you instrument that?
[04:25] Carlos Rivera: yes we can add a routing policy: low-confidence responses go to human review queue. confidence threshold can be tuned during pilot.
[04:32] Maya Chen: any thoughts on multilingual model strategy? try a single multilingual model versus language-specific fine-tuning?
[04:40] Dr. Lena Park: prefer single model if accuracy for KO/ES stays acceptable; if not we'll look at small language-specific adapters.
[04:48] Carlos Rivera: we'll add per-language slices in the evaluation and report per-lang metrics.
[04:53] [04:53] -- MID CALL NOTE: reference deck shared (link) and sample prompt spreadsheet emailed --
[05:00] Akash Patel: curious about baseline: do you have recommendations on the smaller fast model for production latency?
[05:06] Maya Chen: for production we often suggest LlamaX-7b-quant (fast, cheap), Mistral-11 for balanced accuracy, and a 13B instruct for hard reasoning. but for clinical domain we may swap in a medically tuned open model if available.
[05:20] Ruth Gomez: are there known issues with Korean for Mistral? some of our prior tests showed tokenization quirks.
[05:27] Carlos Rivera: tokenization can cause issues; we'll log tokenization ratios and consider byte-level tokenizers or small adapters.
[05:34] Maya Chen: another option is to evaluate a small domain-tuned adapter on top of the mid-sized model — that often improves domain-specific phrasing without the full cost of a larger model.
[05:44] [05:44] -- BENCH PLAN DETAIL --
[05:45] Carlos Rivera: bench plan bullets: (1) run 3 models across quant/fp16 where available; (2) dataset: 2GB sanitized sample + 200 labeled success set; (3) simulate 8 concurrent users with token distribution provided; (4) collect latency p50/p90, cost per req, macro-F1, hallucination rate, schema compliance; (5) per-language slices EN/ES/KO and aggregated.
[06:07] Ruth Gomez: will you include a reranker or verifier step?
[06:10] Carlos Rivera: yes we'll have an optional reranker pass to test precision improvements and report delta in cost/latency.
[06:16] Maya Chen: to close — recap of next steps: lena to share labeled set and sample corpus by 12/08; maya to prod bench plan and ephemeral cred instructions; carlos to run bench and deliver reporting by 12/12; follow-up week of 12/15.
[06:32] Akash Patel: legal and security will follow up on DPA/KMS; i'll loop them in after we see the bench report.
[06:38] Ruth Gomez: thanks all.
[06:40] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and action items.
[06:43] [END]
